messages:
marta: Quick sync — we need a decision on an 'on-demand burst credits' add-on for Dedicated customers. Accounts A and B are asking for short-term extra capacity without moving to a bigger commit. Key questions: pricing approach, per-customer caps, console gating, and contract language for exceptions.

sam: Customers mostly want 24–48h bursts, sometimes multi-day. They prefer a credits model they can pre-buy or charge-to-account. Main ask: allow a one-click burst from the console, or via API.

jules: Finance viewpoint — prefer prepaid credits or committed top-ups (auto-topup). Pricing should be intentionally premium vs reserved capacity so it doesn't cannibalize committed revenue. Ballpark: 2.5x reserved unit price or dynamic based on current utilization. Need clear overage rules.

anika: Eng notes — we can support on-demand bursts with moderate effort. Work items: quota service changes, billing event hook, short-lived autoscale pool, and console UI. Est 3 sprints to get a minimal safe rollout (feature-flagged). We also need a hard per-tenant cap to protect cluster capacity.

ben: Legal — two items: (1) Burst capacity cannot carry Reserved SLA guarantees; must be explicit in contract and UI ("burst capacity not covered by Reserved SLA"). (2) Need export-control and usage restrictions included in the add-on terms. Also propose a short consent checkbox during purchase.

billing-bot: Billing system note: current model supports prepaid wallets + usage events. To support postpay bursts we'd need invoicing adjustments and credit checks.

sam: For GTM, customers want a simple UX: buy N credits -> credits deduct per vGPU-hour. They also want a monthly cap to avoid runaway spend. Suggested default cap: 500 vGPU-hours per burst purchase, configurable up to account limit.

jules: Default cap of 500 vGPU-hours seems sensible for starters. Finance would like a selector: prepaid credits, auto-topup threshold, or invoice-on-use for large enterprise only.

anika: Technical config example (proposal):

```
burst_addon:
  model: credits
  unit: vGPU_hour
  default_cap: 500
  lifetime: 30d
  price_per_unit: 3.50  # USD per vGPU-hour (example)
  sla: none
```

marta: I like that config. Two follow-ups: (A) rollout criteria — internal beta with 3 accounts + canary 10% of Dedicated traffic; (B) launch checklist: billing integrations done, console flow + checkbox, contract amendment drafted.

ben: I'll draft the contract amendment language. Draft to include: no SLA for bursts, billing final at invoice, and explicit customer acceptance during purchase.

anika: Eng estimate update: MVP (feature-flag, console, billing event) = 3 sprints; production polish (metrics, quotas, rate-limiting) = +2 sprints. Need product + sales to fund initial infra cost.

sam: Sales will pilot with Accounts A/B and push for a configurable ceiling. We can accept the 2.5x multiplier as starting price.

jules: Finance asks for telemetry to track migration impact vs reserved purchases (to ensure we don't erode commits). We'll require a 90-day review window after launch.

marta: Action items: @anika build spike for quota+billing (owner: anika), @ben draft amendment (owner: ben), @jules provide pricing floor/ceiling and reporting needs (owner: jules), @sam line up pilot accounts and success criteria (owner: sam). We'll reconvene next Tue.

sam: +1 to owners. Also: add a wallet UI reminder: "Buying burst credits does not change Reserved commitments." :information_source: 

marta: Thanks all — marking this thread as the source of truth for the burst credits workstream.
